content.text: Confirmed via additional searches ("examine", "books", "access") that every access reference is service-delivery or license/security language, not an audit right. Resubmitting the compliant finding.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: No audit right binding the Customer exists in this Agreement, so there is nothing for the AUDIT rule to constrain and no redline is warranted. Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "examine" and "books" returned zero hits, and a full read of the single operative section (§§ 1-14, p0000-p0074) confirms Kubient has no right to audit, inspect or verify AP's usage, books, systems or accounts. Every "access" reference is unrelated to auditing: p0001 is an ordinary cooperation/access covenant so Kubient can deliver the Services; p0002 is AP's inbound licence to the Auction Platform; p0025 restricts AP from granting third-party access to the Service; and p0035/p0045 are database-security representations. There is accordingly no on-site or remote system-access audit right, no self-certification mechanic in § 6 (Use of Service), and no inspection hook in § 12 (Confidentiality). Because AUDIT is protective of the customer, this compliance-by-absence sits at or better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, off-site, Vendor's cost, no system access); the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because no audit clause exists to carry frequency limits, which is not a defect. Separately noted for a different rule and out of scope here (opposite direction): Impressions are defined as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), yet AP has no verification right against Kubient - a gap in our favour to pursue under any vendor-side records/audit rule.
